title: docs(core,react): the two @examples teaching getDataConfig read the shared record source (objectui#7798)
body:
Fixes #7798

Two doc blocks prescribed, in a copyable `@example`, a line that no reader outside two
plugin files can write:

```
const dataConfig = useMemo(() => getDataConfig(schema), [schema]);
```

`getDataConfig` is exported by nothing. It survives only as a **file-local wrapper** in
`packages/plugin-map/src/ObjectMap.tsx:135` and `packages/plugin-grid/src/ObjectGrid.tsx:444`,
so outside those two files there is no module to import it from — the prescribed line does
not compile for any new caller.

Both examples now spell `dataConfig` the way the **live call sites** spell it, which is the
judgement PR #7797 applied to `navigation-overlay.tsx`: follow the live call sites, not
another doc block.

### One measurement that strengthens the card's premise

The card recorded `plugin-map` / `plugin-grid` as surviving hand-copies and left open
whether they are "deliberate residue or a missed leg". Measured on this tree, they are
neither: **both already delegate their ladder to `resolveRecordSourceConfig`** —
`ObjectMap.tsx:174` and `ObjectGrid.tsx:453` both end in `return resolveRecordSourceConfig(schema);`,
keeping only the array-shorthand head above the shared call. So all live sites obtain this
value through the one shared producer; two of them merely wrap it under a local name. That
makes `resolveRecordSourceConfig` unambiguously the spelling the examples should teach, and
it is a reading, not an assumption. It does **not** change the card's defect: the name
`getDataConfig` is still exported by nothing.

⛔ Neither wrapper is touched by this PR.

---

## The diffs — comment lines only

```diff
diff --git a/packages/core/src/utils/record-source.ts b/packages/core/src/utils/record-source.ts
@@ -68,7 +68,7 @@
  *
  * @example
  * ```ts
- * const dataConfig = useMemo(() => getDataConfig(schema), [schema]);
+ * const dataConfig = useMemo(() => resolveRecordSourceConfig(schema), [schema]);
  * const objectName = resolveRecordSourceObjectName(schema, dataConfig);
  * ```
  */
```

```diff
diff --git a/packages/react/src/hooks/useNavigationOverlay.ts b/packages/react/src/hooks/useNavigationOverlay.ts
@@ -210,7 +210,12 @@
  *
  * @example
  * ```tsx
- * const dataConfig = useMemo(() => getDataConfig(schema), [schema]);
+ * import {
+ *   resolveRecordSourceConfig,
+ *   resolveRecordSourceObjectName,
+ * } from '@object-ui/core';
+ *
+ * const dataConfig = useMemo(() => resolveRecordSourceConfig(schema), [schema]);
  * const { handleClick, isOpen, selectedRecord, mode, close, width } =
  *   useNavigationOverlay({
  *     navigation: schema.navigation,
```

`record-source.ts` needs no import line — the file **is** `@object-ui/core`, and its example
is now byte-identical to the `resolveRecordSourceConfig` example seventy lines below it in
the same file. `useNavigationOverlay.ts` names the import, matching PR #7797's shape, so the
line it teaches is copyable as written. The surrounding prose already carries the rule and
is left to carry it, rather than being restated.

**File count**: 3 changed, read from the recorded base `a617bb8d3` (`git diff --stat BASE`),
not a two-dot `origin/main..HEAD` range.

## Type-check readings — through turbo

`type-check` `dependsOn ^build`, so it is run through turbo, not as a bare package script.

| command | tasks | exit |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `turbo run type-check --filter=@object-ui/core --concurrency=2` | 3 successful, 3 total (1 cached) | **0** |
| `turbo run type-check --filter=@object-ui/react --concurrency=2` | 6 successful, 6 total (1 cached) | **0** |

⚠️ **An unmet prerequisite, reported as such and not as a result.** The first attempt used
`pnpm --filter @object-ui/core type-check`, which runs the package script **directly** and
bypasses turbo's `^build`. It produced ~20 `TS6305` ("Output file `packages/types/dist/index.d.ts`
has not been built from source file") plus two cascading `TS7006`/`TS2322`. That is the
dependency declarations not having been built — **not** a type error in this change. Through
turbo, which builds them first, both packages are clean.

## `check:doc-example-readers` re-check — still green, ledger still empty

```
OK  80 documented symbol(s), 3944 call site(s), 11 slot(s) where a call site delegates to a shared reader — no @example hand-spells one.
```

exit **0**. `KNOWN_HAND_SPELLINGS` is untouched and still `new Map([])`; no stale-row error,
which is what the gate prints when a ledger row names a defect it no longer finds.

**The green is a reading, not an absence.** `--list` shows the edited block among the pairs
the gate actually compared:

```
useNavigationOverlay.navigation <- resolveRecordSourceObjectName  (3 call site(s))
useNavigationOverlay.objectName <- resolveRecordSourceObjectName  (3 call site(s))
```

The gate's own collapse guard (`files < 200 || readers < 5 || documented < 5`) also passed.
Its pin test `scripts/__tests__/check-doc-example-shared-reader.test.ts` was run because this
change moves the gate's **input population** — it adds `resolveRecordSourceConfig` as a newly
visible documented symbol in `useNavigationOverlay.ts`, which the gate then compares and finds
nothing on: **22 passed (22)**, exit 0.

⛔ `scripts/check-doc-example-shared-reader.mjs` is **not modified**. Its condition (a) requires
the example to call a symbol the repository exports, so `getDataConfig` never formed a pair and
this class was invisible to it by construction. That narrowing is deliberate and is left alone;
the fact is recorded on the card, which is where it belongs.

## Census: which other `@example` teaches `getDataConfig`?

**Zero outside this PR's surface.** A JSDoc-block scan over every tracked `.ts`/`.tsx` under
`packages/`, restricted to lines inside an `@example` section, finds exactly **2** — both of
them the two fixed here:

```
@example lines mentioning getDataConfig: 2
  packages/core/src/utils/record-source.ts:71  (@example at :69)
  packages/react/src/hooks/useNavigationOverlay.ts:213  (@example at :211)
```

Nothing outside the surface, so no card is filed for this census.

**Measured but deliberately not fixed** (running prose, not a copyable `@example`, and outside
the repair this card authorises): `record-source.ts` still names `getDataConfig` at `:28`, `:50`
and `:65`. `:28` is a **verbatim quotation** of the published contract face — the `.describe`
text on `objectql.zod.ts:656` — and editing a quotation so it no longer matches its source
would be worse than leaving it. `:50` and the `@param dataConfig` at `:65` describe what callers
hand in, which remains literally true of the two wrapper sites. The gate's own documented limit
2 ("prose outside a fenced `@example`") is the same boundary. Flagged here for triage rather
than changed in passing.
